description:
Elixir's rule (elixir_clauses.erl:157-166, :190-191 in ../elixir 1.20.4): a pattern's pins resolve only against the prematch snapshot, the variables bound before the pattern began. For a def head that snapshot is empty, so `def eqp(a, ^a)` is "undefined variable ^a. No variable \"a\" has been defined before the current pattern". For a fn head it is the enclosing scope. Guards read the prematch plus their own clause's bindings; a bitstring size in a match reads the prematch or an earlier segment of the same binary, so a sibling parameter is "undefined variable \"n\"".

fz today: `PatternPinnedInput.input` is written by one post-build loop in guard_dispatch_from_surface (pattern.rs:285-298) matching pin names against clause 0's variable parameters. That binds pins only in programs Elixir rejects (`def eqp(a, ^a)` called from a guard; a guard naming another clause's parameter; `def take(n, <<s::binary-size(n), _::binary>>)`), and the same programs fail on the ordinary call door with "entry dispatch pin has no runtime argument operand". Meanwhile the one VALID use of a pin bound to an input is unimplemented: a single-clause lambda is lowered through entry dispatch with its captures prepended as inputs (jobs/dispatch.rs entry_source_patterns), and `x = 1; same = fn ^x -> :same end; same.(1)` fails on every door. Multi-clause lambdas work only because they take the body-level dispatch with the lexical fallback.

Change:
- SourcePatternRows carries the prematch: the names bound before the pattern begins and which input delivers each. entry_source_patterns fills it with the capture prefix; a def has none; case/receive/with/callsite/exhaustiveness rows pass it empty.
- The producer binds a pin at creation (new, pin_for_name) when its name is in the prematch. The post-build loop and its two stale comments (pattern.rs ~820-825, ~892-895) are deleted. A guard helper is a def: its prematch is empty, its pins never bind.
- GuardArgumentId, PatternGuardBindings.pinned and their plumbing on three doors (jobs/native.rs ~3300, ir_interp/dispatch_exec.rs ~546, native_codegen/receive.rs ~1241) and in canon are deleted; a helper plan carrying any pin is refused with UnknownPinned.
- The entry planner reports every unbound pin as a diagnostic in Elixir's words, through emit_entry_dispatch_error: the head-pin form for ^name, the plain "undefined variable" form for a guard name or a size name.

Fixtures: head_pins_nothing (three invalid shapes, diagnostics pinned on three doors; includes the cross-clause guard name both with a live and with a dead second clause) and lambda_pins_capture (single-clause `fn ^x`, `def pick(x), do: fn ^x -> :same end`, and the multi-clause form; oracle twin). The four pinned receive fixtures stay untouched.

Folds fz-acn.9 (a sibling-parameter size is not a demand bug; it is this diagnostic) and fz-acn.10 (a pin in a head is this diagnostic). fz-tqd.1 is deleted: the clause-0 rule no longer exists. Out of scope, own ticket: a lambda whose bitstring size names a captured variable (capture collection never inspects a field's size expression, jobs/body.rs ~4667).
title: Pins bind from the prematch at creation; the helper pin half and the post-build loop are deleted
